~/workspaces/blender-supermarket · 2026-09-06 · Blender 4.5.13 LTS · blender-mcp addon 1.6

Freshmart Build

A railway-station supermarket you can walk through in Blender: 26 × 22 m of floor, seven gondola runs on a real planogram, 93 fictional-brand SKUs with printed labels and price tags, chillers, checkouts, produce and signage. Built end to end through the Blender MCP server, exported to USD for Isaac Sim.

MCP

Capability test results

Because a running Claude session cannot hot-load a newly added MCP server, a small stdio client (scripts/mcpcall.py) spawns the identical uvx blender-mcp process and calls its tools. Everything below went through that path, i.e. the same code your next Claude Code session will use.

ToolResultWhat was learned
list_tools28 toolsserver spawned with uvx, connected to the addon (protocol 5, addon 1.6, Blender 4.5.13)
disable_telemetryOFFthe server ships with prompt/code/screenshot collection on; switched off for this machine
get_scene_infoOKreturns object list, counts, materials; needs a user_prompt argument in this release
execute_blender_codeOKran the whole builder in 5 staged calls; each call is a fresh namespace, 180 s timeout per call
get_viewport_screenshotOKPNG of the live viewport; used for every visual check in this session
search_polyhaven_assetsOKcapped at 20 alphabetical results, so the Poly Haven API was queried directly to pick assets
download_polyhaven_asset3 assetsfloor_tiles_08 and white_plaster_02 (2k PBR) as materials; wide_street_01 (2k HDRI) as the world
set_texture / get_object_infonot neededthe builder assigns the imported materials itself and scales their Mapping node
Sketchfab / Hyper3D / Hunyuan / Poly Pizzanot exercisedneed API keys or generate meshes; candidates for real carts, people and props later

Quirks worth knowing

  • Per-call namespace. Variables and functions do not survive between execute_blender_code calls. Import your script as a module (sys.path.insert + import build_supermarket) so state persists; exec(open(...)) loses it.
  • 180 s per command. The addon and server both time out at 180 s, so long builds are split into stages. The whole store takes about 4 s, so this never bit.
  • Poly Haven temp files vanish. The addon loads textures from /tmp and deletes the files. Pixel data stays in memory; the builder saved it into assets/textures/ and repointed the images.
  • Zero-user datablocks are purged on save. The imported floor and wall materials had no users and disappeared from the first saved file. They are pinned with a fake user in scenes/supermarket_base.blend now.
  • Normal maps unconnected. The importer links Diffuse and Roughness only; the builder wires nor_gl through a Normal Map node.

Gondola runs are 6 bays × 1.25 m along Y, pitch 3.05 m (1.9 m clear aisle). Every run has promotional end caps front and back.

Fixtures, to real dimensions

  • Double-sided gondola: 2.0 m tall, 0.57 m base deck at 0.17 m, upper shelves 0.47 m deep and 30 mm thick with a 42 mm ticket rail, uprights every 1.25 m, pegboard back panel, kick plate and top cap.
  • Shelf heights are derived per category from the tallest product on each level (0.28 m minimum pitch): cereal gets four shelves, canned goods and personal care six.
  • Wall units (single-sided, 2.2 m): beer & wine on the left wall, bakery on the back wall. Reach-in chillers with glass doors, handles and LED strips (dairy); open multidecks with canopies (drinks, dairy).
  • Front of store: four checkout lanes (belt, scanner glass, POS screen, card terminal, lane light with number sign) with impulse shelves, entry gates, basket stack, nested wire-mesh carts, chip dump bin, promo pallets stacked with shrink-wrapped cases.

LOOK

Renders

ROAM

Walking around in Blender

The scene is open in the Blender window on the desktop, viewport in Material Preview with scene lights and world. Hover the 3D view and press Shift+` for walk navigation: WASD to move, mouse to look, Tab toggles gravity (eye height preset to 1.65 m, speed 2.5 m/s), Shift to run, Esc to stop. Numpad 0 looks through the active camera; the fly-through Cam_Walk runs 510 frames from the entrance through aisles 4 and 6 to checkout lane 2 and out the exit (press Space).

Collections mirror the store: Structure, Fixtures/*, Products/* and PriceTags/* per gondola or unit, Signage, Lighting, Cameras. Hide PriceTags or Lighting if the viewport gets slow. Products are collection instances of the prototypes in the excluded Prototypes collection: edit a prototype mesh or material and every instance of that SKU updates.

Next steps for simulation

  • Reference supermarket.usdc in a stage, then add colliders: convex hull on GRP_Products, triangle mesh on GRP_Fixtures and GRP_Structure. Colliders on instanceable prims are applied on the prototype, which is what you want for 25k products.
  • Map userProperties:sku and category to semantic labels for Replicator ground truth; the slot ids give planogram compliance labels for free (expected SKU per shelf position).
  • Products are static Xforms; make the ones the shelfbot handles rigid bodies (mass from the catalog weight) and leave the rest static.
  • PET bottles use transmission; if RTX real-time looks noisy, swap their prototype material for an opaque tinted plastic in Blender and re-export.
  • The shopfront HDRI is not exported (world material conversion off); use a dome light in Isaac.
PIPELINE

How the store is generated

catalog.py93 SKUs, dims, colours, prices
→
gen_planogram.pylayout + shelves + facings → planogram.json
→
gen_labels.pyPIL labels, tags, signs
→
build_supermarket.py13 stages, headless or via MCP
→
supermarket.blend25.6k objects, 196 prototypes
→
render_shots.py · render_walkthrough.py · export_usd.pystills, MP4, USD

Everything is regenerable: change a product in the catalog, a category assignment in the planogram tables, or a fixture dimension, and rebuild in a few seconds. The base file scenes/supermarket_base.blend only holds the Poly Haven materials and HDRI.

Limits of this first version: products are procedural stand-ins (no scanned real-brand geometry), there are no people or clutter on the floor, produce is spheres in crates, and the wire carts and baskets are simple. The MCP’s Sketchfab, Poly Pizza and Hyper3D tools are the obvious route to real carts, trolleys and scanned products when you want them.
RUNBOOK

Recurring commands

Same content as RUNBOOK.md in the project folder.

1. Start / stop Blender with the scene (MCP socket auto-starts on :9876)

~/workspaces/blender-supermarket/scripts/launch_blender.sh              # GUI on DISPLAY=:0, tmux session "blender"
~/workspaces/blender-supermarket/scripts/launch_blender.sh scenes/supermarket_base.blend   # empty base (only textures + HDRI)
tmux attach -t blender      # console output;  Ctrl-b d  to detach
tmux kill-session -t blender
ss -ltnp | grep 9876        # is the addon socket up?

2. Claude Code ↔ Blender MCP

claude mcp list                                   # "blender: uvx blender-mcp" must be listed (user scope, ~/.claude.json)
claude mcp add -s user blender -- uvx blender-mcp # re-register if missing
BLENDERMCP_ADDONS_DIR=~/.config/blender/4.5/scripts/addons uvx blender-mcp install-addon   # re-install/upgrade the addon

2. Claude Code ↔ Blender MCP

cd ~/workspaces/blender-supermarket
uv run --with mcp scripts/mcpcall.py --schema                                    # list tools + args
uv run --with mcp scripts/mcpcall.py get_scene_info
uv run --with mcp scripts/mcpcall.py execute_blender_code '{"code":"import bpy; print(len(bpy.data.objects))"}'
uv run --with mcp scripts/mcpcall.py get_viewport_screenshot '{"max_size":1400}' --save renders/viewport.png
uv run --with mcp scripts/mcpcall.py download_polyhaven_asset '{"asset_id":"floor_tiles_08","asset_type":"textures","resolution":"2k"}'

3. Regenerate the store (catalog → planogram → labels → scene)

cd ~/workspaces/blender-supermarket
python3 scripts/gen_planogram.py     # layout + per-bay shelves/facings  -> scripts/planogram.json  (edit GONDOLAS/WALL_UNITS/CHILLERS here)
python3 scripts/gen_labels.py        # PIL labels, price tags, signs     -> assets/labels, assets/signs
# headless full build (≈4 s) from the base file that holds the Poly Haven materials + HDRI:
blender -b scenes/supermarket_base.blend --python scripts/build_supermarket.py -- --all --save scenes/supermarket.blend
# or rebuild inside the running GUI through MCP, stage by stage:
uv run --with mcp scripts/mcpcall.py execute_blender_code '{"code":"import sys,importlib; sys.path.insert(0,\"/home/manishsaini/workspaces/blender-supermarket/scripts\"); import build_supermarket as B; importlib.reload(B); B.build([\"clear\",\"structure\",\"library\",\"gondolas\"])"}'
uv run --with mcp scripts/mcpcall.py execute_blender_code '{"code":"import sys; sys.path.insert(0,\"/home/manishsaini/workspaces/blender-supermarket/scripts\"); import build_supermarket as B; B.build([\"walls\",\"chillers\",\"front\",\"produce\",\"signage\",\"lighting\",\"cameras\",\"render\"], save=\"/home/manishsaini/workspaces/blender-supermarket/scenes/supermarket.blend\")"}'

5. Renders

cd ~/workspaces/blender-supermarket
blender -b scenes/supermarket.blend --python scripts/render_shots.py -- --samples 200 --res 1920x1080            # all cameras, Cycles/OptiX
blender -b scenes/supermarket.blend --python scripts/render_shots.py -- --samples 64 --res 1280x720 --cams Cam_Aisle   # quick check (~15 s)
blender -b scenes/supermarket.blend --python scripts/render_shots.py -- --eevee --samples 32 --cams Cam_Overview       # EEVEE still
blender -b scenes/supermarket.blend --python scripts/render_walkthrough.py -- --res 1280x720 --samples 24            # renders/walkthrough.mp4
scripts/pipeline_bg.sh &  tail -f logs/pipeline.log      # USD export + all stills + walkthrough in one go

6. Export for Isaac Sim (USD)

blender -b scenes/supermarket.blend --python scripts/export_usd.py            # -> export/supermarket.usdc (+ export/textures/)
